Shared contract (coordinator-owned, read first; it wins over anything else):

# Phase 4 contract: short reports, rollup, monitor view (release 1.55.0, already pinned)

Owner: coordinator. Workers read this; they never edit it. Dependency-free Node ESM, Apache-2.0 SPDX header, style of the existing tools modules.

## The short report

A worker's report is one JSON object with exactly these keys, nothing else:

```json
{"status":"complete","summary":"...","files":["..."],"risks":["..."],"followups":["..."]}
```

- `status`: `complete` | `blocked` | `failed`.
- `summary`: non-blank string, at most 500 characters.
- `files`: array of declared output paths the worker changed (each must be one of the job's outputs; no duplicates; may be empty).
- `risks`, `followups`: arrays of non-blank strings, each at most 200 characters, at most 10 items each (may be empty).

## `tools/reports.mjs` (new)

```js
export const REPORT_KEYS // frozen ['status','summary','files','risks','followups']
export const REPORT_STATUSES // frozen ['complete','blocked','failed']
export const SUMMARY_MAX = 500, ITEM_MAX = 200, LIST_MAX = 10;
export const REPORT_PROMPT_LINE // exact text below
export function validateReport(value, { outputs = [] } = {}) // -> { report: frozen copy | null, errors: [string] }
export function legacyReport({ status, error, result, outputs = [] }) // -> report object plus legacy: true
export function rollupRun(state, { top = 10 } = {}) // -> compact rollup object
export function renderRollupText(rollup) // -> string
```

`REPORT_PROMPT_LINE` (exact): `Finish with exactly one JSON line and nothing after it: {"status":"complete|blocked|failed","summary":"at most 500 characters","files":["changed declared outputs"],"risks":["short risk"],"followups":["short follow-up"]}. Use exactly these five keys. This replaces any other final-line format above.`

`validateReport` errors (one string per problem, in this order of checking; stop adding after 5):
- not a plain object: `report is not an object`
- missing key: `missing key <k>`; extra key: `unexpected key <k>`
- `status must be complete, blocked or failed`
- `summary must be a non-blank string of at most 500 characters`
- `files must be an array of declared outputs` (also for an undeclared path: `file not in outputs: <path>`; duplicate: `duplicate file: <path>`)
- `risks must be at most 10 non-blank strings of at most 200 characters` (same wording for followups)
Valid -> `{ report, errors: [] }` where report has exactly the five keys (summary trimmed).

`legacyReport` (used when a worker gave no valid short report in a non-strict job):
- `status`: the job record status mapped: complete -> complete, blocked -> blocked, anything else -> failed.
- `summary`: first non-blank of: `result.summary` (string), `result.notes` joined with `; ` (array of strings) or string, `error`, `status`; truncated to 500 characters (ending with `...` when cut).
- `files`: `result.files_changed` or `result.filesChanged` (arrays), filtered to declared outputs, deduped; else `[]`.
- `risks`, `followups`: `[]`. Adds `legacy: true`.

`rollupRun(state, { top })` reads a run's saved state (`state.id`, `state.status`, `state.jobs[]` records with `id`, `status`, `agent`, `error`, `report`, `reportErrors`, `usage`, `costUsd`, `startedAt`, `finishedAt`, plus `state.createdAt`/`state.finishedAt` if present) and returns:

```js
{
  id, status, total,
  counts: { complete, failed, blocked, timeout, cancelled, skipped, queued, running }, // every key present, zero when none
  lanes: { <agent>: jobCount },             // only agents that ran or were assigned
  spend: { costUsd, costReportedJobs, tokens }, // costUsd rounded to cents; tokens = sum of usage.total_tokens (or input+output when total absent)
  files: { changed, jobs },                 // distinct paths across reports' files; jobs with >=1 file
  reports: { short, legacy, invalid, missing }, // invalid = jobs with reportErrors; missing = no report at all
  attention: [{ id, status, agent, summary }], // jobs not complete, plus complete jobs with reportErrors; failed/timeout first, then blocked, then others; summary <=160 chars from report.summary, else error, else status; at most `top`
  attentionMore,                            // count left out
  risks: [{ text, count }],                 // deduped exact text (trimmed), sorted by count desc then first seen; at most 5
  followups: [{ text, count }],             // same, at most 5
  elapsedMs,                                // finishedAt (or now) minus createdAt/earliest startedAt; null if unknown
}
```

Size budget: `JSON.stringify(rollupRun(state))` for a 300-job run with long summaries, 300 risks and 300 followups stays under 4096 bytes. `renderRollupText` stays under 40 lines for any run. Text format:

```
Run <id> - <status> - <total> jobs - elapsed <duration>
complete N - failed N - blocked N - timeout N - cancelled N - skipped N - queued N - running N
lanes  codex N - cursor N
spend  $X.XX (N jobs reported cost) - tokens N
files  N changed across N jobs
reports  N short - N legacy - N invalid - N missing
attention (shown of total):
  <status> <id> (<agent>): <summary>
  +N more: swarm inspect <id>
risks:
  Nx <text>
followups:
  Nx <text>
```
Omit the attention/risks/followups blocks when empty. Durations use the same format as `formatDuration` in tools/monitor-view.mjs (import it).

## Runner (`tools/swarm.mjs`)

- New optional top-level manifest field `report` and job field `report`; the only allowed value is `"short"` (else refuse `report-invalid-mode`: `report must be "short"`). A job is strict when its own `report` is `"short"` or the manifest's is. Apply at the same point job types are applied: a strict job gets `report: "short"` set on the job and `REPORT_PROMPT_LINE` appended to its prompt (`\n\n` + line, once; idempotent).
- Every adapter's built-in final-line instruction (codex base prompts asking for `{"files_changed":[...],"notes":[...]}`, the cursor prompt, claude shell/CLI worker prompts, the API adapters' instruction for the envelope `result` object) must, for a strict job, ask for the short report instead (for API agents: the envelope's `result` object is the short report). Non-strict jobs keep today's prompts byte-for-byte.
- After each worker attempt that ran (status complete, blocked or failed from the worker), take the worker's final object: for worktree writers (codex, cursor) the resolved envelope result; for every other agent the parsed final message (for API agents, the envelope `result`). Then:
  - Valid short report: `record.report = report`. If report.status is `blocked`, the job is blocked (error `blocked: <summary>` up to 300 chars), same as today's blocked handling. If report.status is `failed` and the job would be complete, the job fails with error `worker-reported-failed: <summary>` (300 chars).
  - Strict job and invalid/missing report: `record.reportErrors = errors` (or `['no final report']`), and a would-be-complete job becomes `failed` with error `report-invalid: <errors joined with '; '>` (300 chars). Do not retry the job for this; it is not a provider failure.
  - Non-strict job with no valid short report: `record.report = legacyReport(...)`; never changes status.
  - Jobs that never ran a worker (skipped, cancelled before start, refused) get no report.
- New command `rollup RUN [--text] [--top N]` (N 1-50, default 10): reads the run's state; prints `JSON.stringify(rollupRun(state, { top }))` or, with `--text`, `renderRollupText(...)`. Unknown run refuses like `inspect`. Add it to the usage/help string.
- `inspect` output gains `report` and `reportErrors` per job when present (no other change).
- `monitor --view`: pass extra fields to the renderer: `lanes` (state.lanes snapshot), `queued` count, `mergeQueue` (state.mergeQueue or null), `integratedAt` (state.integratedAt or null), `spend` ({ costUsd, tokens } as in rollup).

## `tools/monitor-view.mjs`

`renderMonitorView` adds, after the usage line and before the table, when present:
- `lanes  codex 3/6 run, 2 queued - cursor paused 1m20s - hermes backoff` (per lane from `view.lanes.lanes`: `<agent> <inFlight>/<concurrency> run` plus `, N queued` when queued > 0; paused lanes show `paused <remaining>` using `until` and `options.now ?? Date.now()`; backoff shows `backoff`). Omit when no lanes.
- `queue  N waiting` (queued job count).
- `merge  <state>`: `view.mergeQueue?.state` when present, else `integrated <ISO>` when integratedAt, else `not integrated`.
- `spend  $X.XX - tokens N` when spend has any cost or tokens.
Large runs: when there are more than 40 jobs, the table shows only jobs that are not complete (at most 40 rows) followed by `... N complete jobs hidden; swarm rollup <id> --text for the summary`. Keep every existing behavior for 40 jobs or fewer.

## Tests

- `tests/reports.test.mjs`: every validateReport rule and error string; legacyReport mapping and truncation; rollupRun counts/lanes/spend/files/reports/attention ordering/top/attentionMore/risk+followup dedupe; the 300-job size budget (<4096 bytes JSON) and <40 text lines; renderRollupText format with and without optional blocks.
- `tests/reports-run.test.mjs` (stub adapters via spawnImpl/fetchImpl as other runner tests do): strict job with a valid report -> record.report saved; strict job with prose or legacy shape -> failed `report-invalid`; strict report status blocked -> blocked; status failed -> failed `worker-reported-failed`; non-strict legacy shape -> legacy report, status unchanged; strict prompt contains REPORT_PROMPT_LINE once and no files_changed instruction; non-strict codex prompt unchanged; `rollup` CLI (spawn the CLI with `--root`) prints JSON and `--text`; a 300-job stub run's rollup stays under the budget.
- `tests/monitor-view.test.mjs`: lanes/queue/merge/spend lines; >40 jobs collapse; <=40 unchanged.

## Release and docs (separate job)

Version is already 1.55.0. New `docs/reports.md` (report shape, strict vs legacy, rollup JSON fields and text example, monitor view lines; say that strict reports become the default for runs created by `swarm go` in a later phase). `docs/manifest-reference.md`: `report` (top-level and job) and a `rollup` command section. README: one short paragraph linking docs/reports.md near the job-types paragraph. skills/project-swarm/SKILL.md: one sentence telling the orchestrator to read `swarm rollup <run> --text` first for large runs and only inspect jobs it lists; keep every section's line and bullet counts unchanged.
